# ui::SpellChecker

Header: `winui/render/SpellChecker.hpp`.

The spell-checking service a text control asks for misspellings, suggestions and autocorrections.

Call it from a text control. The library implements it, and a test installs TestSpellChecker.

A control doesn't call the system spell checker itself. The window installs a checker with Window::set_spell_checker() (non-owning) and hands it to the focused control through [Element::sync_spell_checker()](../tree/element.md#sync_spell_checker). The library's checker uses the system's spell checking and adds what the system leaves to apps: it picks the language from the keyboard layout, and it reports the user's two typing settings through [highlight_enabled()](#highlight_enabled) and [autocorrect_enabled()](#autocorrect_enabled).

Example: 
```cpp
// A text control asks the window's checker. An element of your own can do the same.
class Note : public ui::Element
{
public:
    void sync_spell_checker(ui::SpellChecker& checker) override
    {
        if (!checker.available() || !checker.highlight_enabled() || checked_at_ == checker.generation())
        {
            return;
        }
        errors_     = checker.check(text_); // offsets into text_, in text order
        checked_at_ = checker.generation(); // moves on when a word is added or ignored
    }

    // On "Add to dictionary" in a context menu:
    static void add_word(ui::SpellChecker& checker)
    {
        checker.add_to_dictionary("libwinui"); // every field re-checks
    }

private:
    std::string                    text_;
    std::vector<ui::SpellingError> errors_;
    std::optional<std::uint64_t>   checked_at_;
};
```

## ~SpellChecker

```cpp
virtual ~SpellChecker() = default
```

## available

```cpp
virtual bool available() const = 0
```

False when no dictionary is installed for the current language. Every [check()](#check) then returns nothing, and a control shows no squiggles.

## language

```cpp
virtual std::string language() const = 0
```

The BCP-47 tag of the language being checked, e.g. "en-US".

## highlight_enabled

```cpp
virtual bool highlight_enabled() const = 0
```

"Highlight misspelled words", the first of the user's two typing settings (see the class comment). A control draws squiggles only while it is on, and applies SpellingAction::Replace without asking only while [autocorrect_enabled()](#autocorrect_enabled) is. Neither setting changes what [check()](#check) returns.

## autocorrect_enabled

```cpp
virtual bool autocorrect_enabled() const = 0
```

"Autocorrect misspelled words": whether a control may apply SpellingAction::Replace without asking. See [highlight_enabled()](#highlight_enabled).

## generation

```cpp
virtual std::uint64_t generation() const = 0
```

Bumped whenever something changed that can alter a previous [check()](#check)'s answer: a word added or ignored, the language switched, a setting flipped. A control caches the generation its errors were computed at and re-checks once this moves on, which is how "Add to dictionary" in one field clears the same squiggle from every other field.

## check

```cpp
virtual std::vector<SpellingError> check(std::string_view text) = 0
```

Every error in UTF-8 `text`, in text order; empty when all is well or !available().

## suggest

```cpp
virtual std::vector<std::string> suggest(std::string_view word) = 0
```

Replacement candidates for a misspelled `word`, best first; empty when there are none.

## add_to_dictionary

```cpp
virtual void add_to_dictionary(std::string_view word) = 0
```

Treats `word` as correctly spelled from now on. The library's checker adds it to the user's own dictionary, shared with every other app that uses the system spell checker.

## ignore_for_session

```cpp
virtual void ignore_for_session(std::string_view word) = 0
```

Same, but only for the rest of this session.

## add_autocorrection

```cpp
virtual void add_autocorrection(std::string_view from, std::string_view to) = 0
```

Registers an app-owned correction: [check()](#check) reports a misspelled `from` as SpellingAction::Replace with `to` as its replacement. The correction lasts for this session in this process and never reaches the user's system-wide autocorrect list. The system offers no built-in corrections, so the table is the app's own.
